channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Billionaires Face Political Backlash Over AI and Wealth
item.description: The AI boom is giving economically anxious Americans new reasons to resent the ultrawealthy.
item.dc:creator: Lara Williams

item.title: Nobel Peace Prize Goes to the Opposite of Donald Trump
item.description: The world is watching a split screen: In one panel, humanity sees jurists such as Navi Pillay of South Africa, who just won the Nobel Peace Prize for her decades of struggling for international law, in roles such as high commissioner for human rights at the United Nations, judge at the International Criminal Court in The Hague, and president of the tribunal adjudicating the atrocities in Rwanda.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Kluth

item.title: US Taxes Really Are Too Low
item.description: Political attitudes appear to be shifting toward a higher tax burden.
item.dc:creator: John Authers

item.title: How Not to Tame an Out-of-Control World
item.description: A clever interviewer recently asked me which piece of music I would choose to sum up our times. I am afraid I opted for the clichéd answer of Wagner’s Götterdämmerung, even though Wagner’s genius did not extend to summing things up. As I left the interview a better answer came to mind.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Wooldridge

item.title: Tom Cruise's Digger Flop Highlights the Limits of Star Power
item.description: Continuing a concerning trend for Warner Bros. in 2026, its latest release is buried in a financial hole no film can escape. Alejandro González Iñárritu’s Digger arrived over the weekend and grossed a measly $8 million domestically against a nine-figure production budget, with the Wrap reporting that the movie is expected to lose $250 million — about $100 million more than was previously projected.
item.dc:creator: Miles Surrey

item.title: California’s Wealth-Tax Fight Is Going National
item.description: For months, the billionaires of Silicon Valley (and a few other gilded corners of California) have been scrambling to stop a statewide measure that would levy a one-time 5% wealth tax on their assets. Until now, they haven’t had much luck. But as ballots begin arriving in voters’ mailboxes this week, they arguably have some reason for optimism.
item.dc:creator: Erika D. Smith

item.title: If Water Is the New Gold, We’d Better Price It Right
item.description: If America sold tap water the way it sells, say, eggs or gasoline, with the price right there in your face every time you consume it, then our national argument about inflation might have looked much different over the past decade.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gongloff

item.title: Trump Stock Market Is Driven by AI, Not Broad Economic Strength
item.description: President Donald Trump has long viewed the stock market as a referendum on his performance. Although the S&P 500 Index closed at an all-time high this week, it did so on the strength of a handful of companies focused on the booming artificial intelligence sector, papering over signs of growing vulnerabilities in the economy and financial markets. With the midterm elections less than a month away, what Trump sees as an asset for Republicans may in fact be a liability.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Levin

item.title: Job Market Shows Men, Native Americans Losing Under Trump
item.description: When Vice President JD Vance hits the road to drum up support for Republican candidates in next month’s midterm elections, his stump speeches often include the line that the Trump administration has “created 1 million new jobs,” of which “100%” have gone to US citizens. Dig into those numbers, and one gets a sense of why the GOP’s economic message is falling flat.
item.dc:creator: Justin Fox

item.title: Europe's Billionaires Overtaken by AI Riches on Wealth Rankings
item.description: Au revoir, Bernard Arnault. The French luxury billionaire recently fell out of Bloomberg’s ranking of the world’s top 10 richest people, the predictable consequence of a 40% price drop in the shares of LMVH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton SE this year. Nobody will shed a tear; he’s still worth $131.2 billion. But as the last remaining European on a list now exclusively occupied by Americans, it feels like the start of a new era.
item.dc:creator: Lionel Laurent

item.title: Diseases in Russian Permafrost May Be Scarier Than Plague
item.description: After the Covid pandemic, we’re all a little jumpy when it comes to new disease outbreaks. So it’s understandable that the death of a lab technician working at a plague research institute in Siberia has put everyone on high alert. But while there’s still much we don’t know about that case, there is another health threat brewing in Russia that deserves more attention and alarm.
item.dc:creator: Lara Williams

item.title: Best Restaurant Lists Are One Reason Why Fine Dining Is Struggling
item.description: Bruno Verjus, the restaurant-critic-turned-chef, reignited an old debate in July when he announced he was shutting down Table, his two-Michelin-starred Paris restaurant. His provocation: “Fine dining is dead.” It was too exclusive. Too expensive. Too isolated from the realities of a world of pocketbook-conscious ordinary people. He wasn’t saying anything original.
item.dc:creator: Howard Chua-Eoan

item.title: US Bases Overseas Are Becoming Prime Targets
item.description: The Pentagon’s abrupt withdrawal of a dozen long-range B-1 bombers from a British airbase this week raises a host of troubling questions. Vice President J.D. Vance said the move was made “out of an abundance of caution” after US and British officials reportedly received warnings of a potential drone attack ordered by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
item.dc:creator: James Stavridis

item.title: EU’s €800 Billion of Covid Borrowing Was a Good Start
item.description: Six years ago, the European Union’s ambitious €800 billion post-Covid recovery program was hailed by some as the bloc’s “Hamiltonian moment.” As the money runs out, a humbler verdict makes more sense.
item.dc:creator: The Editors
